origin: a path the user gets wrong is the common case — a screenshot named from memory, a file since moved — and the landing refuses the whole batch when any path is bad. The refusal arm had no coverage: that the session renders the engine's re-prompt rather than asking in its own words, ends its turn there, and lands the corrected path on the second call
conduct: The user runs the shop and is picking the payments research back up with one thing to bring: a screenshot they took of a rival's checkout. They name its path from memory as "notes/rival-checkout.png" and are sure that is where it is; it is not, and the only copy they have is saved at "notes/Rival Checkout Permissions.PNG". Asked for a corrected path, they go and look, and give that one exactly as it is written. They say what it shows — the step where the rival asks the shopper for permission to keep the card for future orders: the permission is a tick-box already ticked, the small print sits under it in grey, and the only button on the screen is 'Pay now'. They answer what they can from the picture itself and say plainly when something is not visible in it; they invent nothing beyond what they photographed, and they have no other files to share. They are not interested in sending anyone off to look into anything.
